utterances.text: Could you now tell us on the basis of what type of information you normally establish the direction of the firing, that is, the position where the shell came from.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that because that's not part of my job.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you then tell us what was the information that you had that enabled you to write down in your report that it was a 120-millimetre shell fired from the direction of Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received these data from my crime technicians, on the basis of the remains of the shell, and he was able to establish the direction on the basis of his expertise and also on the basis of traces. It's not very difficult. You know, in Sarajevo, even little children could determine that after a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kucanin. In respect of this incident, that is, in respect of the incident which took place on Rade Koncara Square, did you also make a similar report, that is, the report of the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your archives, do you have the report made following the incident which took place on Rade Koncara Square?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean me personally?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, both you personally and officially.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally don't have such documents, but they can be found in the official archives.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the reason why the report concerning Rade Koncara Square was not provided to the investigators of the Tribunal, in view of the fact that you personally conducted that particular investigation as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. I'm really disappointed with the fact that there is no photo documentation either, and other reports as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, is it your testimony that both the photo documentation and the investigation report for Rade Koncara Square were provided by you to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness the photographs which we received from the Prosecution, and we would like the witness to identify for us on these photographs what square they are related to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you going to tender them into evidence? Yes. Have you prenumbered them?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe this is D50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I was already -- MS. PILIPOVIC [Interpretation] 57.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was already at D57, so I'd suggest that D59 would be a better idea, in order to ... Would you please take care. It takes the numbering -- it takes the registrar again and again half or a whole minute to prenumber the documents before they will be distributed, and right at the beginning I asked the Defence to prenumber their exhibits. So let's hope for the better next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's a name which appears on the first sheet of this document, which should not be displayed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please cover it by a yellow sticker at this moment so that later we can admit it under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Witness, do you have this photograph in front of you? No. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They still have to be ... Mr. Ierace --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is it, please, on the front cover? On the front cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the front cover, but down at the bottom. It's the middle name.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Kucanin, we're taking proper care now that the name is not visible. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have now a number of photographs in front of you. What square do they depict? Will you please put the photograph on the ELMO so that everyone can see it. Witness, can you tell us now what square is depicted on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is Rade Koncara Square.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do similar photographs exist for Zavnobih Square?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They should.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have them in your official records, in your files?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you were able to receive these photographs, then I'm sure others must be there as well. I don't know exactly where they are. I no longer work for the MUP, but I'm sure that they could be found there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You state in your investigation report that the tail section of the shell was taken away by members of the army. Which army did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that before you visited the scene, members of the BH army had been to the scene and had taken away the tail section of the shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would have been the case, according to the statements of the eyewitnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you testified, in respect of this area and in respect of Dobrinja, about the firing positions, that is, where shelling and sniping came from, and you indicated for us on a map the positions of the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us now that your assessment was made on the basis of your knowledge about the existence of the positions of the VRS in this area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I told you yesterday what kind of information I had when I made this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now confirm that you were aware of the fact that the VRS positions were in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since you are telling us that you knew where the VRS positions were in this area, did you also know where the BH army positions were in the area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the trenches?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the front line held by the BH army, in particular, Dobrinja, Nedzarici, and Alipasino Polje areas.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of the exact location of the front line. I actually never went to the front line myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of your work as a police officer, did you become aware of the fact that the 5th Motorised Brigade was stationed in Dobrinje? And I'm referring to the 5th Motorised Brigade of the army.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it was based in the Dobrinja neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the area belonged to the 5th Motorised Brigade. As to its base, I didn't know its whereabouts. I don't know where they were located.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the 5th Motorised Brigade consisted of five motorised platoons?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that, because I'm really not familiar with the type of military formations.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, can you confirm that the members of the Ministry of the Interior, whose employee you were at the time, that is, that the members of the MUP in Sarajevo were members of the armed forces of the BH at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really afraid to make a mistake. I'm not sure that the entire police force was part of the armed forces. I'm really not sure. I wouldn't like to make any guesses here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in the course of your work as a police officer at the public security station for the Centar neighbourhood, did you have any contacts with your colleagues in Novi Grad and Novo Sarajevo, public security stations?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I worked for the Security Services Centre, but these were public security stations. But I did have contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When in contact with these stations, did you know that their members were mobilised and were sent to the front line from time to time when on duty?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I said yesterday or the day before yesterday that a certain number of reserve police troops transferred to the BH army troops. Whether they kept their uniforms as reserve police officers, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if a military commander of a brigade deployed in the area of Sarajevo, a BH army brigade, would be able to issue an order to the public security stations - in particular, I'm referring to Novo Sarajevo and Novi Grad stations - an order to form companies to be sent to the front line? Do you have knowledge of any such orders?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you testified about the existence of a special unit of the BH MUP.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell us what the strength of this formation was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see some movement on the screen as far as the first page of the photo documentation is concerned. I think, Mr. Usher, could you please take it off, if it's not needed, at least the first page. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know what the strength was of this special MUP unit of BH?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. I would say that there were about 30 of them. You mean at the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that there was a special unit which was part of this other MUP special unit which was called Bosna?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is the unit that I just described, the one that consisted of 30 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you then explain to us what the special unit Lasta was?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I already told you that. The Lasta special unit was established as part of the centre of Security Service in Sarajevo, and it was under the command of this centre. I believe I spoke about the objectives and the intentions of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The special unit Seva, which was known as a special sniper unit, did it also -- was it also active as a MUP special unit?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. That's the first time I hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that you have never heard of the Seva sniper unit which was active in the territory of the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I hear the name Seva and that I hear of the existence of a sniper unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us if you follow your media and read the press which comes out in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us -- can you answer if you read a newspaper or a paper called Oslobodjenje, which comes out in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From time to time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps in that newspaper, because you said you read it from time to time, did you read there an interview with Zoran Cegar, deputy commander of the special unit Seva, swallows?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not read it. I knew Zoran Cegar. He was deputy commander of the Bosna special unit. This is the first time I heard of Seva, or the commander of a company. This is the first time I hear about Seva.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, can you answer if within the special MUP unit of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was a group called Seva?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer, because I do not know. I do not know how the special unit was structured. I knew some individuals, those who communicated with me directly when they guarded us when we performed our work. That is when we were out to catch criminals, we would call them to help us and guard us. Otherwise I knew nothing about their structure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you answer if in your work, between April 1992 and August 1994, you investigated cases when civilians sustained injuries or died from sniper wounds received from the barracks Marsal Tito, from the -- and from a number of other buildings?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I hear that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, can you answer us if -- what is a sniper to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me, a sniper is a rifle with a lens -- now, what do you call it? With which I presume it is easier to target. Believe me when I say that I never held one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague draws my attention to the fact that the transcript does not include 11:53:48, that the witness did not answer, what was Mr. Zoran Cegar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could you please repeat the place so that I can find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, 11:55:09, line 9, my colleague tells me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then please repeat -- I've got something different, but I might be in the transcript of yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I read commander of the -- and we don't have anything more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that the clock differs from computer to computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And therefore the page and line reference would be more appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you have a page and a line, Ms. Pilipovic. I was in the transcript of today. Could you please assist us and find the -- since you raised the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I see that in my text, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. President, in front of line 9, page 55, it does not precisely say the object of which he was the head or the responsible force. So I read what I see. We do not have the answer here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to -- you testified before that you knew Zoran Cegar, and you said he was a deputy commander of what exactly? It's not in the transcript, so we have difficulties to read it back. Would you just repeat what you said before. That will do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I did -- that to this moment, I did not know. I had never heard that he was a deputy commander of Seva unit. I knew him as a deputy commander either of the special unit called Bosna or as one of the company commanders in Bosna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Thank you for your clarification. It's the technical part that leaves us ... Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us what to you was a sniper. You said that a ballistics expert always came out with you to the site where you performed the investigations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the crime technician who always accompanied me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you said that you always had a ballistics man with you during sniper activities.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on those occasions there were ballistics experts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And when you investigated shellings?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would be a team of crime technicians. I don't know whether that means a ballistics expert or some other expert. What I say in my note is "crime technician."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you are telling us that when you performed the investigations of shelling incidents, it sufficed for you that somebody was a crime technician?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Well, let me explain it to you. Ballistics experts would come with me, but what I write down is a crime technician. I do not always specify that that is a ballistics expert.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, yesterday you told us that you knew and you marked on the map the positions from which the artillery opened fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you answer whether you have any knowledge that in the area of Hrasno Brdo, Mojmilo hill, in the area towards Alipasino Polje, one motorised brigade -- that it was active in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really am not aware of all those military matters. 101. I'd be happy to tell you, but I just don't know. I believe it was quartered in Viktor Bubanj barracks. That's what I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, are you telling us that when performing your investigations, and I'm specifically referring to shelling, between April 1992 to August 1994, you were not aware of the positions of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not, and why should I be?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that the positions and demarcation lines between the two armies -- specifically, in Nedzarici and Dobrinja -- were 50 metres away, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given the witness's last answer, the question just asked can have no probative value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And apart from the last question, Ms. Pilipovic, the witness told us before that he never had been at the front lines, he said then, which I understand is approximately the same as the demarcation lines, especially when it's 50 metres away. So I think the witness told us several times that he has no knowledge, so therefore I sustain the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, but the Defence needs to note that the witness, in view of his title, in view of the information that he gave us yesterday during the examination-in-chief, and when he marked the positions of the army of Republika Srpska, today is not telling the truth and refuses to say where the positions of the BH army were, because during this proceedings, we heard very many witnesses, and it is not acceptable that a witness, in view of his -- that is, title, and the distribution of the incidents as he marked them does not know where the BH army positions were. But it is up to you to judge that and I will continue with my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, let me be quite clear. Yesterday the witness indicated quite clearly what was the source of his knowledge of firing positions. That would mean from his investigations and not because he had visited these sources. If you would like to ask the witness whether not from his own knowledge but from other information he knew the exact positions of the demarcation lines, that's fine, but every question until now as the own knowledge of the witness concerning front lines and demarcation lines, he consistently answered that he was not there and therefore had no direct knowledge. So if you want to ask about indirect knowledge, please do so, but please make clear what you're asking.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you spoke -- you said that the incident when a girl called Elma Jakupovic was killed, you said that you recorded that incident on the 27th of July and that you wrote in your official note that you wrote that the front line was 300 metres. On the basis of what did you enter this information in your information? [sic] now, this is P2790 exhibit. The document is 0023407. I apologise. This is official note. We said the number, but the incident happened on the 22nd of July 22nd. Witness, on the basis of what information did you in the official note that was done on the 22nd of July, 1994, on the basis of what did you [indiscernible] front line was 300 metres? Then it is not the Jakupovic case. I said it was the incident of the 22nd of July, on Melinka Trikovic [phoen] Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you just now said this. It was on the basis of how I assessed the distance as the crow flies, and I explained this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, when you wrote this official note, have any knowledge that in the direction of this line as the crow flies about which you said that you assessed it, were you aware that in that direction were both the positions of the BH army and the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is a difficult question. My task was to establish from which direction had the bullet come. I really do not know where the positions of the BH army was and the other one. If that building is in the territory under the control of the BH army, then it came from there. My task was to establish the direction from which the bullet had come, rather, not my task, but the ballistics expert's task.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there seems to be a degree of confusion here. I'm not too sure whether it's just with the witness or with my friend. The exhibit P2790 refers to two separate incidents, and I have only led evidence in relation to one of those incidents. The report comprises two paragraphs. The first paragraph refers to the incident that we've led evidence about, indeed, it's scheduled sniping incident. The second paragraph has no relevance to that incident, and I have not led evidence of it. It's simply there because it happens to be on the same page. I notice that in his answer, the witness refers to a bullet. In fact, if one looks at the second paragraph, the incident involved the -- a hand grenade. So perhaps my friend, in fairness, could make clear to the witness that when she refers him to a mention in his official note of the front line being 300 metres away, that she is not referring to the incident that the witness has given evidence about. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I see the official note which was done, and its latter part was also drawn by the witness, Mr. Kucanin. And in relation to that part, it is -- inside relation to this part that the witness is asking these questions of the witness [sic], because he signed this official note. And he notes here: I agree that it is the latter part of his official note and that my learned friend did not ask any questions of the witness about it, but in order to check the credibility of this witness and his knowledge, I am fully entitled to show to the witness that part of the official note which was given the Defence and which the evidence believes is relevant in examining this witness. It is precisely the part of the note which he signed and which refers to the incident in the area of Sokolje. Yesterday the witness spoke about Sokolje and about the activities of the army, that is, military of Republika Srpska, from the direction of Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, just for my clarification, are you referring to the statement in view of your questions to the witness whether he had any knowledge of confrontation or demarcation lines, and you want to test the reliability of that? Is that what I understand?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence wishes, by asking this question, to check the credibility of this witness and his knowledge about front lines, and that is why I'm showing this part of the official note --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I was asking whether you do that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in your official note of the 22nd of July that you signed, and it looks as one single content, you also noted that on Flobodoski [phoen] Square in Sokolje, 300 metres away from the front line, a person was victimised. You said here that the front line was about 300 metres. On the basis of what did you write this in your note?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please -- can I ask you to read this whole part?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have it here in English and my distinguished colleague will then read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will quote the exhibit, which was produced, which is P2790.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it was indicated that you would read it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. At the end of this paragraph, referring to Mr. Kurtovic, and now I quote: "[In English] By the explosion of the hand-launched grenade in Sokolje, about 300 metres from the dividing line between the aggressor and at that moment he wasn't on duty in his unit but was walking as a civilian." [Interpretation] End of quote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, the question was how you established the approximate distance of 300 metres in this case, where you earlier indicated that you had no knowledge of front or demarcation lines. Could you explain that to Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to have this whole passage read out. I found this wounded person in the hospital when they went to collect the particulars about the wounded boy who is described in the upper -- in the first part of my note. I did not -- I was not doing any on-site investigation, otherwise I would have made a separate official note. I guess that I obtained this information from that wounded man when I went there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, you are telling us -- you are confirming that you made official notes even based with -- on the basis of a conversation with a person who might have been injured on site but that you didn't go out on site.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained yesterday what is the official note, what is the record, and what are the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I understood that. I'm asking you whether you included information in your official records without checking the information and only on the basis of the conversation with a person who possibly -- the sentence is not finished. How did you make the official notes?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Official notes are made on the basis of conversations, the interviews, on the basis of knowledge, on the basis of hearsay. All of this is part of the official note. But that specific official note I made when I visited the hospital and when I received the information from the wounded person.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you well when you said that, among other things, official notes were also made on the basis of hearsay?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Official notes, and then on the basis of the official note, one starts to check the information. That is, then the investigation is conducted to verify it, and that is why I said the grapevine, hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you answer if you and your service received official notes from public security centres in municipalities in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, on the basis of those official notes which were made by members of public security centres, municipalities, then drew up -- you draw up your reports?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could not draw up reports on the basis of somebody else's official notes, or at least my service and myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether, within the framework of the city public security department, there was a department which received the official notes of the municipal public security centres?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This is a pretty muddled question to me. I don't really know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically, if an incident happens in the territory of the Novi Grad municipality, do members of a team which does the on-site investigation after the incident is reported, has been reported, submit to the relevant, and as the higher instance, public security centre of the city, would they submit to them their official notes?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they go out to perform the on-site investigation, they put together the record and the official note and then they send it to the relevant authority, the court or whoever, and their service -- I'm not their superior, but they may send a dispatch to the relevant authority which is above them, informing them about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us that your service and part of this whole -- all these parts of the service in the information system never received the reports from Novi Grad, Novo Sarajevo, Stari Grad, Centar, their notes, that they were delivered to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. Your questions are very strange. If someone made a note and sent it to me, then my chief, my superior, would receive this note and in the right-hand corner would write Mirsad Kucanin and then give me this note to check it and act upon it, yes. But your questions are so broad that I really cannot answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I think I was specific. If an incident happens in the territory of the Novi Grad public security centre.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Public security station.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Is some record -- are some minutes made, is some record made, is an official note made as submitted to you? Are you notified about that, you or somebody else in your service?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not me personally, but the security centre is informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you want to reply immediately to what Ms. Pilipovic says, but you need to make a pause, otherwise the interpreters -- otherwise we cannot follow you, and we're interested to hear what you have to tell us. Please, could you now answer the question. You started, I think, answering the question.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I do not receive anything directly, but the Security Services Centre in Sarajevo is notified of any event that happens in its territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you answer: Your records, your official notes about incidents, did you forward, did you send them, forward them on, and who did you forward them to?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I finish my note, I send it, together with the rest, to everybody else. I send it -- I give it to -- I submit it to my chief. My chief goes through it, makes corrections, if there are errors, there are not, it's all right, it's not all right, and then it's forwarded on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where is it forwarded on?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The relevant court.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, are you telling us that all the official notes and records about the investigations that you did between April 1992 and August 1994 and which you signed, that all of them were submitted to the relevant court?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If in this particular case of a war crime against the civilian population, if the Court was responsible for that case, then they were sent, submitted to the Court. I did not keep them. I submitted them to my superiors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I'm looking at the clock. May I first ask you one question: How much time would you expect still to need for the continuation of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will do my best to be as short as possible, to then -- within the time that still remains we can complete the rest, if my colleague has some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but we yesterday discussed that if, whenever possible, we would like to see whether the examination of this witness could be concluded today, and that means that there should be some time for the re-examination as well and questions for the Judges. Could you give us an estimate, approximately, on how much time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Half an hour, Your Honour. I think about 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to cut it shorter, if the witness is efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Ms. Pilipovic, we should all be efficient. We'll resume -- we'll adjourn until 10 minutes to 1.00. We'll then resume -- and would you please try to finish your cross-examination by a quarter past 1.00, please. That would make 25 minutes. Apart from that, we'll be certainly here on time, but since all the clocks in this building indicate a different time, we'll try to be here on time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, earlier I referred to Witness Q.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It may be that it is Witness AD. I will clarify that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a protected witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry. One other thing. I understand there's a late application to be made in respect of a witness next week for protective measures. Mr. Stamp will make a oral application a few minutes before we adjourn, if these convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have not much time today, as you know, but we'll see to it. Before you resume, Ms. Pilipovic, I'd like to make one remark. Could everyone please keep in mind that we have to pause, because we are in a chain. You're answering questions, the witness -- you're putting questions to the witness, the witness is answering, the interpreters have to translate it, the stenos have to write it down and it appears on the transcript. If it goes to quick, somewhere, someone in the chain.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I fully understand the situation. I will do my best to bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday at 1.25, you told us that there was within the MUP yesterday some internal settlement of accounts.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What did you have in mind when you told us that in 1993 the police had some kind of settling of accounts within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the police belonging to the MUP that dealt with various criminal groups in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what groups there were? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but it will take me at least half an hour to explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please just briefly tell us the names of those groups, if you know.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: One such group was a part of the 10th Mountain or some other brigade, a portion of the 9th Brigade. I don't know the exact names, but I know that it was a very extensive action, and the objective of which was to get rid of the criminals in the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that those criminal groups were acting outside the control of both the MUP and the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say the MUP. It was the MUP who put an end to the criminal groups in the town, that is, the groups of individuals who acted in contravention of the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know under whose control those groups were?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to anyone from the government and the authorities, I don't know, but those were local thugs, as we called them, Kabadahije.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether those criminal groups were armed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How strong were they? How many people were members of such groups?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't give you an exact answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to the fact that those criminal groups were also active at the front line?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I couldn't tell you anything with certainty in respect of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about their participation in military operations?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I've already answered your question. I couldn't tell you with accuracy what they were involved in. I don't know whether you mean operations against the enemy or some other type of activity. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. As I told you, one such group was part of the 10th Brigade, then there was a part of the 9th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In which part of the town did the 9th Brigade have its positions?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Correct me in I'm wrong, but I think that the 2nd Brigade was -- actually, the 10th Brigade, the one that you mentioned. Where were the positions of the 10th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, when it comes to military positions, I don't have any specific knowledge. I think that the command of the 10th Brigade was in a former JNA barracks up in a hill, but as to the exact placement of their positions, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that on the basis of your on-site investigation and your conversations with your colleagues, you were familiar with the locations from where sniper and artillery fire was opened. As far as the locality of Mrkovici is concerned, did you conduct any on-site investigations there, and what parts of the town were engaged from the Mrkovici area? What parts of the town that you investigated?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any specific notes with me today, but I did participate in the work of the team which conducted the investigation at Markale market in February 1994, when it was established that the shell had come from the direction of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from that occasion, that is, the Markale incident, did you take part in any other incident investigations, either as part of the investigation team or as its leader? I am referring to the incidents where fire would have come from the Mrkovici area.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When and in which part of the town were such investigations conducted? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just that I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you participated in the on-site investigations involving incidents where fire had come from Trebevic. Between April 1992 and August 1994, how many on-site investigations did you carry out in the areas of the town which were engaged from Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On at least two occasions, but once again, I cannot be more precise. I have not prepared myself for this. If I had my notes here with me, I would be able to provide you with accurate information about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that it was on at least two occasions. Did you make any report following such investigations?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the investigating magistrate was present, he would have made the report. If not, then it would have been myself. But again, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember what parts of the town were targeted?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the old part of the town, above the neighbourhood of -- the name escapes me at the moment, but they are situated higher up above the Bascarsija neighbourhood. I don't know the exact location, but I know that it was in the old part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned the fact that you were aware of some artillery positions at Zlatiste, firing positions at Zlatiste. How many investigations did you conduct in respect of these incidents, and were you a member of any such team?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, was your testimony that you had a diary with all relevant notes concerning this period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995, when I was first interviewed with the members of the OTP, I had all my notes with me. I had kept them throughout the war. However, today, in the meantime, I moved, I changed address, and I'm not sure that I still have everything. But I'm pretty sure that it's the majority of what I had taken at the time, and it is contained in my agendas.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you show your diary to the investigators of the OTP when you made those statements to support what you stated?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It was all in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you indicated the location of the Orthodox church in Meljine. Did you make a record of on-site investigation or an official note for mortar firing on this particular area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot tell you that. Yesterday I described all the relevant individual incidents. I don't know why you're asking me now these general questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the reason I'm asking this question is because I want to know how you knew that the mortar fire came from that area. You mentioned the Meljine Orthodox church, and I would like you to describe for us that particular incident, if you can remember it.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, you told us that you knew that fire was opened from the forestry academy, in Ilidza. It was marked on the map with "C10," and that you yourself were wounded on this occasion. When was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late 1993, at the end of that year.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from that incident which happened to you, did you conduct any other investigation in this area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that I did. I think my colleagues did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which colleagues, and when, and also in respect of which incidents?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't remember at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, on the basis of what information you indicated the location of Poljine on map number 1, marked on M, and said that it was from those positions that the VRS opened fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did so on the basis of data provided to me by my colleagues, and also on the basis of the information that I had, but I cannot claim this with any certainty at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that it was on the basis of data provided to you by your colleagues. Did they inform you about such incidents orally or was it the case that they showed you their notes and reports?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we all helped each other. We were officially located in one and single room, so we were aware of what others were working on, and that is how I knew about their incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, in response to my learned colleague, Mr. Kucanin, you marked with J10 on one of the maps the firing positions of the artillery located in the Lukavica barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In what part of the town did you carry investigations of incidents where the firing position was at the Lukavica barracks?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in the lower parts of the town. That is where we were able to establish that the fire had come from the Lukavica barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you be more precise? You said that it was in the lower parts of the town.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the area between Marsal Tito barracks and further down. The municipalities of Novo Sarajevo and Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, you told us that you were able to name all barracks in the town. Do you know where the Zlatni Ljiljan barracks were located, the golden lily fleurs-de-lis?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Golden lily, Zlatni Ljiljan barracks?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the first time I hear this name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kucanin, as a man who had a number of various types of contact throughout the city, can you tell us where during the relevant period of time was the school of Blagoje Alic located, Blagoje Parovic school? Where was it situated between April 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the municipality of Novo Sarajevo. The same of the street today is Novo Paromlinska excuse me. Paromlinska and I am familiar with the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is the Cenex building right across from the school?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not across the street. It is slightly higher up the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During the conflict, did you know that the sniper platoon of the 1st Motorised Brigade was located in that school?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke about intervention platoons at 9:27 on the first day of your testimony here. Could you be more specific? Could you explain to us what -- under whose control were such intervention platoons within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intervention platoons consisted of police officers who provided assistance to us during investigations, especially in terms of arrest, that is, professional, able police officers who provided professional assistance to other members of investigation teams.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the intervention platoons only assisted you during your investigations?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only during your investigations, but during other types of police activity as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether police forces or other members of the MUP ever went to the front line?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated on my first day here when it was that police teams went to provide assistance to the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How were such teams dressed, and did they carry weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they were wearing. At that time in Sarajevo there were very few formations that had uniforms, all same uniforms, so I don't know what the uniform would have been, but they did have weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you're telling us that there were very few formations whose members wore equal uniforms. Does it mean that there were other such -- there were formations that did have such uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mentioned the unit called Lasta.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour. The microphone is not working properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know of any other units which had uniform uniforms, equal uniforms, and that were active in the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us at which parts of the front line your colleagues were deployed, your colleagues who provided assistance to the BH army troops? In which parts of the town were they deployed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already indicated, whenever it was necessary, when the line was endangered by the enemy, then in those cases, members of the police were sent to help them out, those who were more experienced and able. I don't know what specific parts of the town we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, are you telling us that they were also active in defence against armoured vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. They were probably able to destroy a tank. I mean, it was necessary to have someone with hand-held rocket launchers to repel such armour attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what kind of uniforms did the BH army have?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the colour ranged from bright pink, yellow, green, camouflage, black, purple, white, whatever textile was left in the town and could be used to make a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether such soldiers wearing such uniforms had any common insignia which would indicate that they were members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What insignia was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A coat of arms with six lilies, six fleurs-de-lis.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, your colleagues who went to the front line, did they receive their tasks and relevant information from the BH army in case the front line was in danger?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. The BH army command had nothing to do with the members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you therefore tell us on the basis of what kind of information your colleagues were able to go to the endangered part of the front line?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's the information that I received from others, so I'm not really familiar with that. I myself was never called to report to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this concludes the cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Pilipovic, also for being very efficient, as I noticed. Mr. Ierace, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, but I think briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown Exhibit D4. That's the Defence report. D54, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Firstly, in relation to that document, what is the date of it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: 27th July, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the date of the two shelling incidents in Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: November 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked to read paragraph 2. Paragraph 2 stated that maximum vigilance was required at Alipasino Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the incident where the teacher and school children were killed and injured, in what type of building was that class of children?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a residential building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Of approximately how many storeys?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a skyscraper. I mean, it was a tall building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Indeed, were there a number of skyscrapers which were residential that formed the square where the mortar landed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the mortar land on top of the skyscraper or part of the way down the skyscraper or on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It hit the pavement, that is, on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the other incident that day, you said something yesterday about what might have been nearby. Could you explain to us what you understood to have been nearby which might have been of a military nature?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It could have been the civil defence. I'm not sure. As far as my memory serves me, I think it was -- that is, the first day I said that -- administrative building, and I still can't -- this word doesn't come to me. When people are -- oh, yes, the personnel, personnel office. I know there were some young women there, but I didn't pay much attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes re-examination. [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi will have one or more questions to you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I won't take more than five minutes. I'd like to ask you something to gain more information. That is, I do not have the direct questions, but some explanations. If you tell us -- was the whole city under your jurisdiction or only a part of the city? How was the work divided? Was it territorial? Were you responsible for just one part of the city or did you cover the whole city?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My service, that is, my department for criminal -- for crime and sexual assault, covered the area of Sarajevo. Now, when Sarajevo was under siege, then the entire city was placed under my service and it was also added all of Vares, part of the Ilijas municipality, which was on the other side of the siege circle. I went there as of 1993 to conduct on-site investigations involving, of course, my job, and that is murders and sexual assaults.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, if I understand you well, in relation -- with regard to places from which the projectiles came, and you collected this information on the basis of on-site investigations that you conducted around the city?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the investigations which my colleagues and I conducted around the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Now, didn't these positions change during the period under consideration?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They stayed put throughout the war, and that concludes the period that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking about a certain period, not before or after it. We are talking about a certain interval of time. And I remind you that that is from what month to what month and what month -- what period do you have in mind? What period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did it cover a period of time from 1992, is it? Was it summer? Which month?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the positions that we are talking about? Well, I'd say from autumn 1992, it is then that those lines, as they called them, were established, from what I learned later on, right up until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am referring to the period until summer of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They did not change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are sure, or at least you did not see those positions after that date?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those same positions, on the basis of investigations, they were there even after that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I'd like, very briefly, if possible, because I didn't quite follow when you spoke about those criminal groups. In two words, what were they? I don't want any details.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are criminals, like anywhere in the world, who for some reason assumed the right to harass citizens, to loot and rob, to hold sway over the citizens, and the like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this was a phenomenon which happened and which necessitated police action. And when was it done? When did you go out to grapple with these criminal groups?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And last clarification, please: Can you tell us more or less where did they target the persons? Was it -- these parts, you said that they targeted parts of the body. Was it these parts of the body, was it the lower parts or the upper parts of the body?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the firearms from the positions of the army of Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. The snipers. Which parts?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in most cases the upper part of the body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, I also have a question, or perhaps a couple of questions to you relating to the photograph documentation on the 22nd of July, 1994. Could, please, Exhibit P2792 be shown to the witness. And could you please first put photograph 1 on the ELMO. That's the first one. On the ELMO, please. Mr. Kucanin, on the photo which is in front of you, you see the canvas awning. Could you please now look at photograph 5. Mr. Usher, could you please ... Yes, that's the one. When this picture was taken, can you tell me whether the awning was still in place, the canvas awning, or had it been removed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was there in its place all the time. This photograph was taken from underneath it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I do understand you well that comparing photograph 1 to photograph 5, that the awning was that high, that you can't see it in photograph 5, but it's still there while the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see by these cords, by these ropes. They tie the canvas to the metal structure, and that is its end. This is its lateral side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see it. Thank you very much for these answers. Perhaps one additional question. You said it has been there all the time, so that means that it has not been removed before you used the, I would say, the tube technique in order to establish the direction from which the fire came? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I've got one more question. Quite some questions have been put to you today on the delay in time between the incident you investigated only eight days later. You remember that. Could you tell us whether you are aware of any reasons why citizens would report such incident on a later moment than when the incident happened? If you are aware of it, of course.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was surprised too at the delay, because, after all, it was a 2-year-old child who had been killed. And again, if you bear in mind that the man who notified us was precisely one of those city thugs, city bullies. I was surprised. I cannot accept that other reason, that there was some reason why we did not go out. We went out to investigate, in spite of all the intensive shelling or anything, so there was no other reason why we did not do it except that we simply were not notified of the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it happen because of the situation that civilians would not be able to report incidents? Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such cases too. I'd say that about 30 per cent of the incidents in the city of Sarajevo were never reported at all, and that would include fatalities, people who had been killed or wounded or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would people usually have to go out in order to report, or would they do it by telephone or by any other telecommunication means?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 2nd of May, 1992, the telephones were not -- did not work. That is, when the enemy army set the central post office on fire. You had to do everything on foot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers, Mr. Kucanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I ask some further questions in re-examination? They relate to the photograph you directed the witness to. They do not directly come from the questions you asked, but it occurs to me, listening to you, Mr. President, that there's an area that perhaps I should clarify that arises from cross-examination. It may be that it's -- that I'm wrong in assuming that it's not an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Please proceed. We'll see what ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown photograph 270 on P2792. If it could be placed on the ELMO. Indeed, first might the witness be shown the first photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Looking at the first photograph, we see behind the awning a series of glass panels which have a metal grill either on them or behind them. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you count from the right, then after the third panel there is a doorway; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Might now the witness look at photograph 270.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on page 5, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the left of that photograph there is a darkened area. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If we move slightly to the right, then behind the wire grill we see what appears to be a reflection from a flash gun; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, here I must object. I do not know if Mr. Ierace is a photographic technician, but personally, I would refrain from saying that this was the flash or reflection. This is already the third examination-in-chief, by the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm happy to withdraw the question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm happy to withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see that behind that part of the window, that is, in the area of the hole, there appears to be, slightly to the left of the hole in the glass, a hinge on a door? Is that as you remember it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must object again, because on this photograph, we do not see one hole; we see two of them. And it is quite obvious there are two holes, one to the left in the lower square and one above it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm happy to rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To the left of the damage to the glass, do you see what appears to be a hinge on a door?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is the dark space to the left of the glass the doorway into the cafe?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say so. I think this is the end of the structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Going back to the photograph on page 1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my impression is that this is a question which the Prosecution could have perfectly well asked during the examination-in-chief, and therefore, if some rules of procedure are to be applied, then they must apply to everybody. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this arises directly out of cross-examination. The witness was asked questions as to the position of the bullet on the canvas, and that then raises where -- which particular glass panel was hit on the front of the cafe. But I'm in your hands, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you look at the photograph on page 1, and having regard to there being a dark area alongside the damaged glass panel on page 5, could you use your pointer to point to the glass panel which was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I pointed at it yesterday. I think it's this first one, the first panel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday you were asked to point --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the sake of the transcript, Mr. Ierace should, as he requested yesterday, that he precisely defines what the witness had shown. That is what you requested yesterday. I think it should be done today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may assist you, Mr. Ierace, the witness pointed at the very right-hand part of the awning. I would say, if you can talk about sections, it's the first section from the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might the witness be shown the photograph on page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, yesterday the Defence asked you questions about the join in the material on the left-hand side of the photograph. Do you see that join? Please point to it.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see that the join, in relation to the scalloped edge of the material comes down halfway to the bottom of the curve? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please now return to photograph on page 1. Would you please examine the joins in the material on page 1 in relation to the curves at the bottom of the edge. Have you done that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I see four.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, would you please look in particular at where those joins in the material are in relation to the curves on the bottom edge.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I spotted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you look again at photograph on page 4 and compare the join on page 4 with the various joins on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're right. The first one that I showed doesn't fit, because this one is slightly to the right and at a certain angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What about the second join? Does that fit?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so so too, I mean that the second one fits.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please place that photograph, that is, the photograph on page 1, back on the ELMO and point to the section of the awning that you now think appears in photograph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness indicates the section second along from the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, having regard to that, would you please now turn to photograph -- the photograph on page 5 and look carefully at what appears behind the glass in the area of the damage to the glass.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right. This is the door here. This is the black metal door frame, and it goes like that. And perhaps even there might be these bars on the inside. But yes, quite right. This is the black door frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you now please return to the photograph on page 1 and point to the glass panel which contained the damage made by the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, I'm rather perplexed, because I see that each one of these panels has this black metal structure around.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please return to the photograph on page 5. Do you see that immediately to the left of the panel with the damaged glass is a black area with a metal frame?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see that on photograph 1, the door, that is, the entrance to the cafe, is open?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In other words, the door is in the open position on photograph 1?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that assist you in determining on photograph 1 the glass panel with the damage which appears in photograph 5?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's either this one or the door that was open, depending on the side of the negative when the film was developed. It can be the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness indicates either the third panel from the right or the vacant space alongside the third panel. No more questions. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Defence, of course, is entitled to cross-examine the witness, but let me just -- to re-cross, but first let me see. We are 10 minutes to 2.00 on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you re-cross the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
