utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you for this. I sort of hesitated because everybody is tired, including the interpreters. I wanted to know whether we could have the witness on Monday, but perhaps we should like -- perhaps we should ask the interpreters whether they would give us a few more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I should have done it, and I intended to do it, and then the registrar came to me and said that she -- she wanted to bring something to my attention as well. So first of all, would it be possible, all knowing that whenever we could conclude the examination of this witness today, I think it would be good for everyone. Would it be possible to continue? I'm looking at the interpreters' booth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your great cooperation. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I will take the same liberty as Mr. Ierace. Thank you. Can I have the photographs on the ELMO, please, number 5, photo number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm now talking about the second square in the second row on the left side. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, would you please put the indicator on that square.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. On the lower left corner, we see a hole. Would you please put the pointer on that hole.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In the opposite corner we see a fracture in the glass. Would you please point to it, that is, to the upper right corner.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that this is also a hole or a fracture, but I will indicate the part in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness briefly pointed to the upper right corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, isn't it true that here we can see a fissure in the glass; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I see several of them, several such lines, several cracks. Perhaps you can help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Can we zoom up a little bit? Can we blow up the square a little bit, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I presume that further cross-examination is limited to the subject which was covered in my re-examination. This appears to go beyond it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, we clearly see -- at least, I do, even without my glasses -- two impacts, one in the upper corner with cracks around it and the other in the lower corner, also surrounded by some cracks; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two points of impact of the bullet? No, I wouldn't agree. I think that the bullet impact is only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, but witness, can you not see --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did ask a question which referred to the impact. My friend objected. I withdrew the question. There was nothing in my re-examination which touched on whether there was one hole or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, during the re-examination you have put further questions to the witness in respect of the place where an impact of a bullet would have taken place on a glass. What, as I see it now, is that Mr. Piletta-Zanin is verifying whether there was one impact or more than one impact. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: For the record, what we see on the screen, and that is blown up, is the second square in the second row of squares. In the glass we see two distinct areas of fracture, one in the upper -- in the lower left corner and one in the upper right corner. I think that this is a sufficiently objective description. Witness, as we see two areas of fracture here, and since you indicated that the bullet hit the target only once, how come -- how did you proceed with the tube that you had? In which hole did you decide to put the probing instrument for the purposes of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that this was not my job, that this was the job of the ballistics expert or the crime technician, but I am sure from this vantage point in time that there was only one hole. This other damage was caused by something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can I conclude that your answer is that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever I knew is contained in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Kucanin, I know that you have been waiting for quite some time and that you have been examined for quite some time as well. I'm quite glad that you came and that you answered all the questions put to you. I'm also glad that at least we could conclude your examination today so that you can return, which of course is important for you after so many days abroad, and especially since your job was endangered. Thank you very much for answering all the questions, because for the decisions this Court will have to take, it's very important that people come and testify of what they know of the events that happened many, many years ago in Sarajevo. Thank you very much. We have to deal with some technical issues again. Mr. Usher, would you please lead out Mr. Kucanin. And Mr. Kucanin, a good, safe trip home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too, Your Honours, and if I was of any assistance, it is really my pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, we really are a bit in a hurry, also because you have got to do other things as well. I suggest that any objections against the admission of evidence will be done Monday morning, so that we'll have then time and we'll not have to hurry, since there might be some matters of principle involved as well. I think the only thing then left is that Mr. Mundis [sic] would like to make a submission as far as the production of witnesses is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps that could wait until Monday as well. There is another issue which is perhaps more important. Mr. Harding has been waiting around to give evidence, but rather than him give evidence on Monday, I respectfully suggest that we allow him to return again to his home and come back to The Hague in, say, two or three weeks' time. I do that because his situation is a little different from someone who is able-bodied, and there's a degree of stress and tiredness involved. So I prefer that we went straight to calling Mr. Besic on Monday, if that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order not to waste anyone's time, the Defence agrees with this solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for your cooperation. Could you please tell Mr. Harding, also on behalf of the Chamber, that we deeply deplore, without blaming anyone for it, that he had to wait a long time and he has to return again. But, well, the trial left us no other possibility. But I'd like you to convey this to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. So we then deal Monday morning with the protection of witnesses. I would like to invite the parties also to express themselves on the 92 bis then perhaps, because we said we'll do it when we have a moment left. Well, it turns out there are hardly any moments left. So I would like also to do that Monday morning to start with, so we might spend the first half an hour with these kind of issues. I thank all the parties for their cooperation. I especially thank the interpreters' booth for helping us out of this rather difficult problem on Friday and making it possible for Mr. Kucanin to return to Sarajevo, and I wish everyone a good weekend. We'll adjourn until next Monday at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
